name: Old Moss Green
lede: Old Moss Green is a dark, yellow-leaning olive, [[moss-green]] without the cool cast most people expect, and over three decades three other names landed on almost the same spot.

sections.title: One spot, several names
sections.body:
The library records Old Moss Green from Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, plate 14 L 2, first recorded in 1905 [1]. Our computed classification gives it a light olive, built on [[moss-green]] but pulled toward yellow rather than the blue-green moss usually shows [1]. The same plate position carries three near-duplicate names recorded in other years: Lizard Bronze in 1892, Palmleaf in 1917 and Romantic Green in 1928, each within a hair of the same hex [1].

The nearest distinct neighbor in the library is [[baby-poop|Baby Poop]], about 4.8 units away by CIEDE2000, with [[silver-fern|Silver Fern]] close behind it [1]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 56, chroma 61, hue 98 degrees, Munsell 8.3Y 5.4/8.3 [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 34 of 23,781 paintings, 0.14 percent, as photographed [2]. It is most over-represented in the 1900s decade, in 5 of that decade's 809 paintings, about 4.3 times the expected rate [2]. Russia accounts for 3 of the 34, its largest share by country [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment test [2].
